content: 1. Co-administration of stiripentol with erythromycin lactobionate can increase the levels or effects of streptomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of sublingual sufentanil (SL) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Co-administration of sublingual sufentanil with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may elevate sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to increased or prolonged adverse effects, including life-threatening respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 5. Both sulfamethoxazole and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 6. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the starting dose of suvorexant to 5 mg at bedtime when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Talazoparib is a P-glycoprotein substrate, and co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to talazoparib. 9. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which decreases the conversion of tamoxifen to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction may be necessary for drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 11. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, so monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness when co-administered. 13. Both erythromycin lactobionate and telavancin prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen when co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 15. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tobramycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Inhaled tobramycin and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to reduce the risk of ototoxicity. 18. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No specific dose adjustment is recommended when tofacitinib is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, but the dose should be reduced if co-administered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 19. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of tramadol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction or adjustment of dosing intervals may be required due to an increased risk of serious adverse events, including seizures and serotonin syndrome. 22. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Both erythromycin lactobionate and trimethoprim prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 24. Triptorelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Both erythromycin lactobionate and tropisetron prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 26. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. 27. Both valbenazine and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate and valoctocogene roxaparvovec both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Medications that may cause hepatotoxicity when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec can potentiate the risk of elevated liver enzymes. Monitor closely and consider alternative medications in case of potential drug interactions. 29. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of valsartan by inhibiting the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and the vardenafil dose should be limited to 5 mg per 24 hours. 31. Both erythromycin lactobionate and venlafaxine prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 32. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of vitamin K1 (phytonadione) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Both erythromycin lactobionate and voclosporin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Both erythromycin lactobionate and voriconazole prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 39. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Reduce zanubrutinib to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt dosing as recommended for adverse reactions. Resume the previous dose of zanubrutinib after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 41. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 45. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 46. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of alvimopan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 47. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of ambrisentan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 48. Amobarbital decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 49. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of amoxicillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 50. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of ampicillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 52. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Butabarbital decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 54. Butalbital decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Clindamycin and erythromycin lactobionate decrease each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 56. Erythromycin lactobionate and clindamycin topical decrease each other's effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 58. Danazol increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 59. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of desloratadine by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 60. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of dicloxacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 61. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 62. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 63. Ethanol decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 64. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of fexofenadine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 65. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of lansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 66. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 67. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of methylprednisolone by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 68. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of nafcillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Bacteriostatic antibiotics may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 69. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of oxacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 70. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of penicillin G aqueous by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 71. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of penicillin VK by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 72. Pentobarbital decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 73. Phenobarbital decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 74. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of prednisone by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. There is a risk of toxic steroid concentrations and altered mental status. 75. Primidone decreases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 76. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of rabeprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 77. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 78. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of temocillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 79. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of valproic acid by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 80. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels of zafirlukast by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 81. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. Decrease the acalabrutinib dose to 100 mg once daily if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 82. Adagrasib and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes, other serious arrhythmias, and sudden death. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, more frequent monitoring is required.
